reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; the rendered redline is byte-identical to p0016 and no counterparty-facing text was generated.

The cited clause does support fallback-level compliance: 'Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice' is a Customer convenience right at 90 days, i.e. the outer edge of the 60–90 day fallback window; 'for any reason' is a recognized phrasing variant of 'for convenience'.

Detection trigger is correctly assessed as not met: the Initial Term is one (1) year with 1-year auto-renewals, so there is no lock-in in a term longer than 12 months, and the mid-Initial-Term bar is symmetric (it equally restrains Kubient), so it is not flaggable against us.

Vendor's convenience right is on exactly ninety (90) days' notice, which sits outside the walk-away trigger ('fewer than 90 days'); that it is not confined to the end of a renewal term is a sub-element short of preferred wording and is properly noted in the rationale rather than escalated.

No early-termination penalty is imposed on the Customer — Kubient is only entitled to fees generated during the 90-day notice period while continuing to perform, which is within the fallback's 3-months'-fees ceiling; the absence of a pro-rata prepaid-fee refund is credibly explained by the revenue-share payment structure in §5 where funds flow from Vendor to Customer.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is explained by the literal-phrase regex missing 'for any reason'; it is a phrasing variant, not evidence of a missing right.
